name: valantic-cx-target
_readme: How valantic draws and assesses CX target architectures: canvas lanes, legend and palette, element and arrow rules, the interface and system tables behind every diagram, SSOT placement per data domain, hub policy, views (as-is, target, delta, data-flow zoom), common anti-patterns and target-option patterns with prerequisites. Best practice, not hard guardrails - a pattern applies where the client's landscape has the element. Every row is reference guidance to be confirmed against the client's own systems and interfaces before it appears in a deliverable.

snippets.reference_persona: valantic CX solution architect who has drawn and defended target architectures for B2B manufacturers and retailers (ERP, PIM, DAM, CMS, commerce, CRM, iPaaS, search, analytics) and judges a landscape by where the single source of truth sits per data domain, whether every interface is a row in a table, and whether the target picture states lifecycle status, decision status and phase for every element
snippets.reference_focus: SSOT placement per data domain and duplicate mastership; every arrow as an identified interface with direction, data objects, style and frequency; hub policy stated and direct links justified where a hub exists (never an empty placeholder hub); lifecycle status (keep, new, replace, retire, open) and decision status per element; manual steps kept visible; undecided systems named by their capability term; one box per deployable system with capability detail in zoom views; as-is, target and delta never mixed; data-flow zooms for the critical flows (product, price, stock, customer, order); the tables (system inventory, interface list, decision log) behind the picture
